title: Star stitch — the five-spoke pull
subtitle: Draw five loops through a single yarn-over to make a raised five-point star
excerpt: Star stitch pulls five separate loops onto the hook and closes them all through a single yarn-over to create a raised star shape. The five spokes radiate from a central yarn-over knot. Worked in rows it creates an intricate-looking fabric that is deceptively straightforward once the five insertion points are understood.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 3 (1888) — star stitch in crochet fabric patterns. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — grouped-loop pulled stitches.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet stitch formed by inserting into five separate positions to draw up five loops, then closing all of them with a single yarn-over pull-through, and finishing with a ch 1 'eye'. Each completed star overlaps with adjacent stars to create a dense interlocking fabric.

heroPrompt: A crochet swatch in pale pink DK yarn showing star stitch pattern, three or four visible stars with their five-loop radiating centres clear, close-up overhead view.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Five loops on hook from five insertion points, about to be closed with one yarn-over pull-through

content.text: works by gathering five loops from five different positions and closing them all at once through a single yarn-over. The five insertion points are: the first chain of the turning chain, the stitch before the starting point, and three consecutive stitches after. The close-all-through creates the raised centre knot of the star, and the single chain 1 forms the eye of the star.
Foundation: chain in a multiple of 2, plus 1.
Insert hook into 2nd ch from hook, draw up loop. Insert into 3rd ch, draw up loop. Insert into 4th ch, draw up loop — 4 loops on hook.
Add one more: insert into 5th ch, draw up loop — 5 loops on hook.
Yarn over and draw through all 5 loops. Ch 1 to close the eye of the star.

For the next star: the last 2 of the 5 loops are shared with the previous star (insert into the eye and the last insertion point of the previous star), then 3 new insertions. 5 loops, close, ch 1. Continue.

items.symptom: Stars are difficult to count — pattern gets lost
items.cause: Missing or misidentifying the five insertion points
items.fix: Place a stitch marker in the eye (ch 1) of each completed star as you go. The eye is always one of the insertion points for the following star.

items.cause: Pulling the five-loop close-all too tightly
items.fix: Draw through all five loops with a moderate tension — firm but not yanked. The star should sit flat, not dome upward.

content.text: Spider stitch uses a similar multiple-loop drawn-up technique but inserts into chain spaces rather than stitches, creating a lacy web effect. Puff stitch is the simpler pulled-loop close in a single position.
